note.explanation: CSS styles HTML elements. A CSS rule has a selector that chooses the elements and declarations that tell the browser what styles to apply.
examples: h1 { color: red; } changes the text colour of all h1 headings to red.
body { background-color: blue; } gives the page a blue background.
note.checkAnswer: A selector chooses the HTML elements to style; declarations give the properties and values.
note.simple: Think of CSS as instructions for how HTML content should look.
note.checkQuestion: In a CSS rule, what does the selector do?
note.title: Styling webpages with CSS
steps: Write a selector for the HTML element you want to style.
Inside the braces, write each property followed by a colon and its value.
End each declaration with a semicolon.
note.answer: CSS styles HTML elements using rules made of selectors and declarations.

options: The selector identifies which HTML elements the rule styles.
The selector gives the value of a CSS property.
The selector links an external CSS file.
The selector creates an HTML element.
mcqs.stem: What is the role of a selector in a CSS rule?
rationales: Correct: a selector specifies which HTML elements the styles apply to.
Incorrect: a declaration gives a property and its value.
Incorrect: the HTML link tag is used to link an external CSS file.
Incorrect: HTML tags create elements; CSS selectors target them.

mcqs.stem: Which is a correctly written CSS declaration?
rationales: Correct: a CSS declaration uses a property, colon, value, and semicolon.
Incorrect: CSS declarations use a colon, not an equals sign.
Incorrect: the property and value need a colon between them.
Incorrect: the declaration is missing its ending semicolon.

mcqs.stem: Which example applies an inline style to a heading?
rationales: Correct: inline CSS is placed directly on an element using the style attribute.
Incorrect: css is not the attribute used for inline styles.
Incorrect: this is not the correct way to apply an inline style to h1.
Incorrect: link is not the attribute for an inline CSS declaration.

options: In the head section, inside a style tag
In the body, inside a script tag
In a paragraph, inside a font tag
In a table, inside a link tag
mcqs.stem: Where does internal CSS go in an HTML document?
rationales: Correct: internal CSS is included in the head section using the style tag.
Incorrect: a script tag is used for JavaScript, not internal CSS.
Incorrect: this is not the method for adding internal CSS.
Incorrect: internal CSS is not placed in a table or link tag.

mcqs.stem: Which CSS property sets the background colour of an element?
rationales: Correct: background-color sets an element's background colour.
Incorrect: font-style controls the style of text, such as italic.
Incorrect: background-position places a background image.
Incorrect: animation-duration sets how long an animation takes.

mcqs.stem: Which property creates space inside an element?
rationales: Incorrect: margin creates space outside an element.
Correct: padding creates space inside an element.
Incorrect: font-size changes the size of text.
Incorrect: background-size controls the size of a background image.

mcqs.stem: Which declaration makes an element a CSS Grid container?
rationales: Correct: display: grid; sets the element to use CSS Grid layout.
Incorrect: font-weight controls the weight of text.
Incorrect: background-color requires a colour value, not grid.
Incorrect: animation-name identifies an animation, not a layout.

options: It gradually changes a property between styles.
It links a CSS file to an HTML document.
It arranges items into rows and columns.
mcqs.stem: What does a CSS transition do?
rationales: Correct: a transition makes a property change gradually instead of instantly.
Incorrect: a transition does not remove an HTML element.
Incorrect: the link tag links an external CSS file.
Incorrect: CSS Grid arranges items into rows and columns.

written.finalAnswer: Use the <link> tag in the <head> section, for example: <link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">.

examTips: A short question may ask for the three ways to apply CSS or the tag used to link an external stylesheet. Name the methods clearly and show the link tag accurately.
A longer question may ask you to explain animation and transitions. Define each, give a relevant CSS example, and explain what the important properties do.

For code questions, marks are commonly earned for the correct selector or tag, correctly written property-value declarations, and the requested final effect. Keep braces, colons, semicolons, and filenames accurate.

yourTurn.question: What are the different ways to apply CSS to an HTML document?
solution: CSS can be applied using inline styles, internal styles, and external styles.
Inline styles are added to an HTML element using the style attribute.
Internal styles are placed in the head section using the style tag.
External styles are written in a separate CSS file linked using the link tag.

explain.title: CSS rules
explain.body: CSS is composed of rules that consist of selectors and declarations. Selectors specify which HTML elements the styles will apply to, while declarations define the specific styles to be applied, including properties and their corresponding values. A rule follows this format: selector { property: value; }.

explain.title: Three ways to add CSS
explain.body: Inline styles go directly on an HTML element using the style attribute. Internal styles go in the head section using the style tag. External styles are kept in a separate CSS file and linked in the head using the link tag.

explain.title: Fonts and backgrounds
explain.body: Font properties include font-family, font-size, font-weight, and font-style. Background properties include background-color, background-image, background-repeat, background-position, and background-size.

explain.title: Layouts, animations, and transitions
explain.body: CSS Grid arranges items in rows and columns; Flexbox arranges items flexibly in a row or column. Margins create space outside an element, while padding creates space inside it. Keyframes define animation stages, and transitions make style changes happen gradually.

mistakes: Writing an equals sign instead of a colon between a CSS property and its value.
Forgetting semicolons between declarations or leaving out the braces around a CSS rule.
Mixing up the three methods: inline uses a style attribute, internal uses a style tag, and external uses a linked CSS file.
Putting the external stylesheet link outside the head section or omitting its rel or href attribute.
Confusing margin (space outside) with padding (space inside).
Describing a transition as an animation without showing the changed style or the transition property.
